Hypothesis: We hypothesize that in HCC under hypoxic stress, HIF activation drives enhanced glycolysis, resulting in elevated lactate production and acidification of the tumor microenvironment. This acidification, in cooperation with lactate binding to its receptor GPR81, instigates polarization of TAMs towards a pro-tumorigenic M2 phenotype while concurrently upregulating CA12, a key factor in macrophage survival and chemokine (e.g., CCL8) secretion. The secreted cytokines, notably IL-10 and TGF-β, then trigger a paracrine loop that induces the PHGDH-mediated serine synthesis pathway in tumor cells, elevating NADPH production and strengthening redox balance to promote resistance to targeted therapies such as TKIs and ICIs. In parallel, AMPK-mediated autophagy may further augment these metabolic adaptations. Advanced methodologies, including single-cell RNA-seq, spatial metabolomics, multiplex cytokine profiling, and CRISPR screening, will be employed to map and validate each step of this cascade, thereby identifying precise nodes for therapeutic intervention.
Abstract: In hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), we propose that under hypoxic conditions, HIF activation upregulates glycolytic enzymes such as HK2 and LDHA, resulting in increased lactate production and subsequent acidification of the tumor microenvironment. The acidic milieu not only facilitates lactate binding to its receptor GPR81, thereby promoting the polarization of tumor-associated macrophages (TAMs) to a pro-tumorigenic M2 phenotype, but it also directly induces upregulation of CA12 in these macrophages, enhancing their survival and secretion of chemokines like CCL8. These M2 macrophages secrete cytokines, particularly IL-10 and TGF-β, which act in a paracrine manner on tumor cells to induce the serine synthesis pathway via upregulation of PHGDH. The resulting increase in serine metabolism boosts NADPH production and supports redox homeostasis, ultimately conferring resistance to targeted therapies such as TKIs and ICIs. Furthermore, we suggest that concurrent AMPK-mediated autophagy may synergize with this cascade to further sustain tumor cell survival under metabolic stress. To validate and dissect this interdependent mechanism at high resolution, we propose using contemporary techniques including single-cell RNA sequencing, spatial metabolomics, multiplex cytokine profiling, and CRISPR screening.
CausalChain: Hypoxia -> HIF activation -> Upregulation of glycolytic enzymes (HK2, LDHA) -> Increased lactate production -> Acidification of tumor microenvironment -> Lactate receptor (GPR81) engagement and CA12 upregulation in macrophages -> M2 macrophage polarization -> Secretion of cytokines (IL-10, TGF-β) and chemokines (CCL8) -> Paracrine induction of PHGDH and serine synthesis in tumor cells -> Increased NADPH production -> Enhanced redox homeostasis -> Therapy resistance (TKIs/ICIs) [+ AMPK-mediated autophagy support]
